st: Pat the halloumi slices dry with paper towels so they brown instead of steam.
Heat a nonstick or cast iron skillet over medium-high heat. No oil is needed in the pan because the cheese releases its own fat.
Lay the slices in the dry pan, leaving space between them.
Cook for [[2 minutes]] per side until deep golden brown and a little crisp at the edges.
Move to a plate and drizzle with [[1 tbsp]] olive oil.
Scatter [[2 tbsp]] chopped mint and the pepper over the top and squeeze lemon juice over it.
Serve right away while hot and soft, with the extra lemon wedges.
Mix the grated onion, [[1 tbsp]] oregano, lemon juice, [[0.25 cup]] olive oil, garlic, [[2 tsp]] salt and the pepper in a large bowl.
Add the pork and lamb chunks and turn them to coat well. Cover and marinate in the refrigerator.
Thread the meat onto long metal skewers, packing the chunks together, alternating pork and lamb.
Heat a charcoal or gas grill to medium heat, or heat the oven to 400°F (200°C) with the skewers on a rack over a pan.
Cook the skewers slowly, turning every few minutes, until the outsides are browned and the meat is cooked through. Pork should reach 145°F (63°C) and be tender; lamb should be at least 145°F (63°C).
Rest the skewers for 10 minutes under foil.
Slide the meat off the skewers and serve in pita with tomatoes, onions and lemon.

ing: or thin sheets of pork fat
st: Soak the caul fat in a bowl of cold water with [[1 tbsp]] vinegar for 10 minutes to soften and clean it. Drain and spread it out flat.
In a bowl, mix the pork, onion, parsley, cinnamon, [[1.5 tsp]] salt and the pepper with your hands until evenly combined.
Cut the caul fat into pieces about 5 inches square.
Shape about [[2 tbsp]] of the meat into a small sausage, set it on a piece of caul fat, and wrap it up snugly so the fat covers the meat.
Thread them on skewers or lay them on a rack. Chill for 15 minutes to help them hold their shape.
Cook on a medium grill or under a hot broiler, turning often, until browned and the inside reaches 160°F (71°C).
Rest for 3 minutes and serve in pita with onion, tomato and parsley.

ing: or leg of lamb, cut in large pieces
st: Heat the oven to 325°F (160°C).
Poke deep holes in the lamb with a knife and press a garlic piece into each. Rub the lamb all over with [[2 tsp]] salt, the pepper and [[1 tbsp]] oregano.
Place the potatoes and tomatoes in a deep roasting pan and toss with the lemon juice and [[0.33 cup]] olive oil.
Nestle the lamb among the potatoes, tuck in the bay leaves and pour in the wine, or water if you prefer.
Cover the pan tightly with parchment and then foil, sealing the edges so the steam stays in.
Bake for about 3.5 hours until the lamb is falling off the bone and the potatoes are soft. Baste once halfway through.
Remove the foil, raise the heat to 425°F (220°C) and roast until browned.
Rest 10 minutes and serve with the pan juices spooned over.

ing: jarred, rinsed well, or fresh blanched
st: Rinse the grape leaves in warm water and trim off any hard stems. Spread a few at a time on a board, shiny side down.
In a bowl, mix the pork, rice, onion, tomatoes, mint, parsley, [[1.5 tsp]] salt, the pepper and [[2 tbsp]] olive oil.
Put about [[1 tbsp]] of the filling near the stem end of a leaf, fold in the sides and roll up tightly like a small cigar. Repeat with the rest.
Line the bottom of a wide pot with a few extra leaves. Pack the rolls seam side down in tight layers.
Pour over the lemon juice, [[2 tbsp]] olive oil and [[2 cups]] hot water. Set a small plate on top to keep the rolls from moving.
Bring to a simmer, cover, and cook on low heat until the rice and pork are cooked through (pork reaches 160°F or 71°C).
Cool for 10 minutes and serve warm with extra lemon.
Combine the pork, red wine and crushed coriander seeds in a bowl. Cover and marinate in the refrigerator.
Lift the pork out of the marinade with a slotted spoon and pat it dry. Save the wine.
Heat [[3 tbsp]] olive oil in a heavy pot over medium-high heat. Brown the pork on all sides in two batches.
Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute. Pour in the reserved wine and scrape up the browned bits.
Add [[1.5 tsp]] salt, the pepper and the cinnamon stick if using. Bring to a simmer, then cover.
Simmer over low heat until the pork is fork-tender and reaches at least 145°F (63°C).
Uncover and cook until the wine has reduced to a thick glaze, about 10 minutes. Serve with rice or fried potatoes.
Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C). Boil the pasta in well-salted water until just short of done, then drain.
Heat [[1 tbsp]] oil in a pan and cook the onion for [[4 minutes]]. Add the ground beef and cook until browned and no pink remains, reaching 160°F (71°C).
Add the tomatoes, cinnamon, [[1 tsp]] salt and the pepper. Simmer until thick.
For the bechamel, melt the butter in a saucepan, whisk in the flour for 1 minute, then slowly whisk in the milk. Cook until thickened, with [[1 tsp]] salt and the nutmeg.
Cool the sauce for 5 minutes, then whisk in the eggs and half the halloumi.
Toss the pasta with the meat sauce and spread it in a 9x13 inch baking dish. Pour the bechamel over the top and sprinkle with the remaining halloumi.
Bake until golden and bubbling on top.
Rest for 10 minutes before cutting into squares.
Mix [[2.5 cups]] flour, yeast, sugar and salt in a large bowl. Add the melted butter, 2 eggs and [[0.5 cup]] warm milk and knead for [[8 minutes]] into a soft dough.
Cover and let rise in a warm place until doubled.
For the filling, mix the halloumi, Parmesan, 2 eggs, mint, raisins, [[0.5 cup]] flour and baking powder into a thick paste.
Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C). Line a baking sheet with parchment.
Divide the dough into 12 balls and roll each into a 4-inch circle. Brush the edges with water and dip the tops in sesame seeds.
Put [[2 tbsp]] of filling in the center of each and fold the edges up to make a square or round pocket, pinching corners to hold.
Place on the sheet, rest 20 minutes, then bake until deep golden brown.
Cool on a rack. Serve warm or at room temperature.
Put the tahini in a medium bowl and stir in the garlic and [[0.5 tsp]] salt.
Add the lemon juice and stir. The tahini will stiffen and look curdled; this is normal.
Add [[0.33 cup]] cold water a spoonful at a time, stirring hard after each, until the mixture turns pale, smooth and creamy.
Thin with a little more water if you want a pourable sauce, or leave thick as a dip.
Taste, then add more salt or lemon juice as you like.
Spoon into a shallow bowl, drizzle with [[1 tbsp]] olive oil and top with [[2 tbsp]] chopped parsley.
Whisk the flour, yeast, sugar and salt in a bowl. Add [[1.5 cups]] warm water and stir into a thick, sticky batter.
Cover and let rise in a warm place until doubled and bubbly.
Warm the honey, [[0.25 cup]] water and lemon juice in a small pan for 3 minutes. Keep warm.
Heat [[4 cups]] oil in a deep pot to 350°F (175°C).
Wet a spoon, scoop a walnut-size spoonful of batter and push it into the oil with a second wet spoon.
Fry in batches, turning, until deep golden on all sides.
Lift out with a slotted spoon, drain on paper towels, then toss in the warm honey syrup.
Pile on a plate and dust with the cinnamon. Serve at once.
